title: The Creator's Passion and the Guarded Tomb
english: Yesterday the earth was shaken and was deliberating about flight, threatening to split apart for its inhabitants. The mountains were being struck, and the rocks were being split. The temple was naked, just as a living being having torn its garment, showing through what it suffered that the holy things had been profaned. The lifeless things perceived the outrage, but those who dared it had unfeeling souls. The elements were indignant; they almost abandoned their order and worked confusion upon everything, had they not perceived the will of the Creator—that he was not being insulted unwillingly.

O strange and paradoxical events! The one who by a word stretched out the heaven is stretched out on wood. The one who bound the sea with sand is wrapped in bonds. The one who gave the springs of honey is given gall to drink. The one who crowned the earth with flowers is crowned with thorns. The one who struck Egypt with the ten plagues and covered the head of Pharaoh with the waters is struck on the head with a reed. The face that the cherubim cannot bear to look upon is spat upon.

And while suffering these things, he prayed for those who were crucifying him, saying, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do” (Luke 23:34). He conquers evil with goodness. He speaks in defense of those who killed Christ, saving them. He dissolves the charge by attributing it to ignorance. He is not angry at becoming the plaything of their drunken violence. He accepts the drunkenness and in love for humanity calls them to repentance.

Why say more? Having gained nothing from his goodness, they shut in a tomb the one whom nothing that exists can contain. They place seals, guarding our salvation for us, and fearing the resurrection they set soldiers as guards at the tomb. Who has ever seen a corpse under guard?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG In diem sabbati sancti u01-rem-early
orientation: Amphilochius continues his contrast between yesterday's cosmic upheaval at the crucifixion and today's hidden victory, now describing the paradox of the Creator suffering and the Jews' fearful guarding of the tomb.

title: The absurdity of guarding a corpse
english: Or rather, who has ever seen a corpse being warred against? Who has heard of an end being disputed, striking fear into those who accomplished it? Who has not taken his enemy's soul? Who has not ended the hatred, satisfied with the death of the hostile one? Why do you fear the one you have destroyed, O Jew? Why are you afraid of the one you killed? Why do you tremble at the one who has departed? Why do you dread the one you put to death? Why are you in anguish over the one you crucified? You have security from the slaughter. Take courage: if the dead man is a mere man, he does not rise. If he is a mere man, you did well to set up the cross. If he is a mere man, he does not speak truly when he says, "Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it" (John 2:19). If he is a mere man, he is held by death. If he is a mere man, why do you seal the tomb, you fool? Wait for the third day and you will see the proof of your own madness. Cease your meddling and you will behold the outcome of events. Cease redeeming according to the truth. Cease warring against God and wounding yourself by the war. Cease insulting the sun of righteousness and thinking you can quench those rays. Cease striving to dam up the spring of life. Cease troubling the rulers and discussing the guard. Cease buying falsehood and stirring up the soldiers.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG In diem sabbati sancti u01-rem-mid
orientation: The preacher continues his direct challenge to the Jew, pressing the paradox that the precautions taken at the tomb betray a fear that Jesus was no mere man.

title: The tomb cannot hold the risen Lord
english: Do not labour to no profit. Do not spend what is yours on impiety. Do not imagine victory against God. Do not pay soldiers to say one thing instead of another. Do not make the crowd sleep beside the tomb. Do not trust in weapons. Resurrection is not hindered by weapons, is not blocked by seals, is not barred by soldiers, is not stolen with money. But do you not believe? Did you not see Lazarus long ago shaking off death as if it were sleep? Did you see how the dead man obeyed the command and the binding did not hinder him? Did you see how he walked with his grave-cloths still on when he heard "Come out" (John 11:43)? Did you see how the voice fitted together the one dissolved by death? The one who had power for those things will have power for these things too. The one who raised the servant will himself rise far more. The one who gave life to the rotting man will not leave himself dead. But the blindness of the Jews is great, and seeing the wonders they do not see. They have eyes but do not see, ears have they and do not hear (Isaiah 6:9-10). For the god of this age has blinded their hearts so that the gospel of righteousness may not shine upon them (2 Corinthians 4:4). But let us leave them for now in unbelief, and let us say with the women around Mary, shaping for ourselves in thought the tomb of the Saviour: "They have taken away our Lord and we do not know what they have done with him" (John 20:2). To him be glory with the undefiled Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG In diem sabbati sancti u01-rem-close
orientation: The preacher is addressing the Jew who sealed and guarded the tomb, challenging him to stop fighting God and to remember the raising of Lazarus as proof that Christ will rise.
